//: Pinned third-party runtimes bundled into the XP POS installer.
Every version here is EXACT and every download is checked against sha256.
That is the whole point: a client box gets no toolchain and no internet, so
whatever is captured here is what runs the restaurant. A floating version
would mean two sites on the same nominal build behaving differently.
To change a version: edit it here, run `build.ps1 -UpdateHashes` to refetch
and record the new digest, then commit BOTH the version and the hash. Never
hand-edit a hash.
An empty sha256 means the artifact has not been pinned yet, and build.ps1
will refuse to use it unless -UpdateHashes is passed.
Node 24 Krypton is the current Active LTS - longer support runway than 22
Jod. Next 16 requires Node 20+, and the env-file flag this install depends
on for its configuration needs 20.6+.
This digest was cross-checked against the official SHASUMS256.txt at
https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.18.1/ and matched, so it verifies the upstream
artifact and not merely whatever we happened to download.
bcrypt and sharp ship N-API prebuilds, which are ABI-stable across Node
major versions, so the runtime we ship does not have to match the one the
developer built on. build.ps1 proves this per build by executing bcrypt
under the bundled node.exe rather than assuming it.
Only mongod.exe is taken. The zip is ~592 MB, but most of the extracted
content is mongod.pdb and mongos.pdb debug symbols (~1.5 GB together) plus
mongos.exe, the sharding router, which a single-node replica set never
uses. The shipped payload is ~61 MB.
SSPL: redistributing this binary in a commercial installer is a licensing
question the owner has accepted. See NATIVE_MIGRATION_NOTES.md.
AVX: MongoDB 5.0+ requires an AVX-capable CPU. Celeron/Pentium N-series
(N3350, N4000/N4020, N5030) will die with Illegal instruction. The
installer must detect this - see Phase 6.
VC++: mongod.exe imports msvcp140.dll and vcruntime140.dll, which are NOT
guaranteed present on a clean Windows 10. vc_redist.x64.exe is extracted
from this same zip for the installer to chain.
mongodump.exe and mongorestore.exe. These are a SEPARATE download from the
server - they have not shipped inside the server archive since 4.4, which
is easy to miss.
Phase 7 depends on these: the XP Thermal Service currently runs backups via
docker exec mongodump and must be repointed at these binaries. Backups gate
go-live, so do not drop them from the payload to save space.
Support tool only. The installer does NOT need it: rs.initiate runs through
the bundled node.exe and the mongodb driver already inside the app bundle
(installer/scripts/rs-init.mjs). Shipped so a technician on site can inspect
the database without downloading anything.
Stock release binary, per the owner's decision. This serves every
LAN-by-IP deployment.
config/Caddyfile.tls (the optional APP_DOMAIN trusted-HTTPS mode) needs a
caddy built with a caddy-dns provider compiled in and will NOT load on this
binary. Producing that variant requires Go + xcaddy on the build machine:
xcaddy build v2.8.4 --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare
BUILD-MACHINE TOOL, not shipped to clients - it Authenticode-signs the
installer and the three WinSW service wrappers.
This is the Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools NuGet package (a .nupkg is
just a zip) rather than the full Windows SDK, which is a multi-gigabyte
system install. Only bin/<ver>/x64/signtool.exe (538 KB) is used, and it
is extracted into .depcache - nothing is installed on the machine.
Fetched only when signing is actually requested, so a developer build
with no certificate never downloads it.
BUILD-MACHINE TOOL, not shipped to clients - it compiles setup.iss into
the installer .exe.
build.ps1 -Package extracts it PORTABLY (/PORTABLE=1) into .depcache and
runs ISCC.exe from there. Nothing is installed to the system: no registry
entries, no Program Files, no PATH changes. A system-wide Inno Setup 6 is
used instead when one is present, and -IsccPath overrides both.
This is auto-fetched for the same reason every other dependency is: the
build must be reproducible from a clean checkout without a human
installing tooling by hand first. Unlike the runtimes below it is a
developer dependency, so it does not affect installer size.
6.7.3 is the current stable 6.x. Inno Setup 7 exists but 6.x is the
mature, widely deployed line. Releases are code-signed (Pyrsys B.V.).
The net461 build (640 KB), not WinSW-x64.exe (17.8 MB, self-contained .NET
Core). .NET Framework 4.8 ships with Windows 10/11 so net461 adds no
prerequisite.
v2.12.0 is the latest STABLE release (Jan 2023); v3 is still alpha.
NOT CODE-SIGNED - Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports NotSigned. The brief
assumed otherwise. Sign the three renamed copies alongside the installer in
Phase 6 rather than shipping unsigned service wrappers.
WinSW resolves its config by looking for a file named after its own exe, so
the payload gets three renamed copies of this one binary.
